title: Rational points of locally separated algebraic spaces are closed immersions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $Z$ an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum] whose relative diagonal is an immersion. Here an immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable morphism whose pullbacks to schemes are immersions in the sense of [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every field extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], put $Z_K=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Every $K$-morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z_K$ is a closed immersion: for every scheme $T\to Z_K$, the pullback $T\times_{Z_K}\operatorname{Spec}K$ is a scheme and its map to $T$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The singleton image of $a$ in $|Z_K|$, with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], is closed. No finite-type or quasi-separatedness hypothesis is imposed on $Z$.

Field base change preserves local separatedness by spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated). Closed immersion means spaces.tex Tag 02YU (definition-immersion).

proof.text: Form $X=Z_K$ as an algebraic space. By local-separatedness permanence its diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is an immersion. The scheme map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is locally separated; composition therefore makes $X$ absolutely locally separated.

source.place: Tags 03KL, 03KQ, 03KY; scalar extension followed by the absolute structure map

proof.text: The locally-separated-space theorem now makes $X$ decent, in the explicit sense that every field-spectrum morphism into $X$ is quasi-compact.

The unique point $s$ of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is closed and has residue field $K$. Since $a$ is a $K$-morphism, its composite with $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the identity. Apply the finite-field-map theorem with $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $L=K$ and the degree-one extension $K/K$. It gives representability of $a$ and finiteness on every scheme test.

The section $a$ is a monomorphism: for any test scheme $H$ and maps $b,c:H\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ with $ab=ac$, composition with $p$ gives $b=c$. For $T\to X$, the projection $a_T:T\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ is also monic: two maps into the fibre product equal over $T$ have equal $\operatorname{Spec}K$ components by this cancellation, so are equal as pairs.

source.place: Tag 08AL, equal-residue-field case; section cancellation written out

proof.text: For every scheme $T\to X$, step 3 makes $a_T$ a finite morphism of schemes and step 4 makes it a monomorphism. The finite-monomorphism theorem makes $a_T$ a closed immersion. This is precisely the required closed-immersion assertion on all scheme tests.

Let $x$ be the image of the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. For every etale scheme test $U\to X$, the point-lifting lemma identifies the inverse image of $\{x\}$ in $|U|$ with the point image of $U\times_X\operatorname{Spec}K\to U$. This image is closed by step 5 and the definition of closed immersion. The definition of atlas topology therefore makes $\{x\}$ closed in $|X|$.

lean.statement: theorem rationalPoint_isClosedImmersion_of_locallySeparated (k : Type u) [Field k] (Z : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (hdiag : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsImmersion p.left) (prod.lift (𝟙 Z.obj.obj) (𝟙 Z.obj.obj))) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (a : yoneda.obj (Over.mk (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))) ⟶ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).op ⋙ Z.obj.obj) : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) a ∧ IsClosed ({schemePointMap a (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)} : Set (Point ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).op ⋙ Z.obj.obj)))
